chunks: Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Mutual separation (mubara'ah) is when a woman says to her husband, 'You are free from any obligation I have upon you, so leave me,' and he leaves her. Except that he says to her, 'If you take back anything from it, then I have greater claim over your marital bond.'
And it is narrated: it is not appropriate for him to take from her more than her dowry; rather, he takes from her less than her dowry. And in mubara'ah, her husband has no right of return over her.

key_terms.ارْتَجَعْتِ: you took back or reclaimed what had been relinquished
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the wife who seeks separation from her husband
key_terms.الْمُبَارَأَةُ: mutual dissolution of marriage through separation by agreement
key_terms.بِبُضْعِكِ: over your marital relation or conjugal bond
key_terms.لَا رَجْعَةَ: there is no right of return or revocation for the husband
key_terms.لِزَوْجِهَا: to her husband, indicating the marital legal relationship
key_terms.مَهْرِهَا: her dowry, the dower owed to the wife in marriage

ai.seo_question: What are the legal rules of mubara'ah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the fiqh of mubara'ah, a form of mutual dissolution of marriage initiated through the wife's renunciation of certain claims in exchange for separation. It also states that the husband should not take more than the dowry from her, and that mubara'ah does not grant him a right of raj'ah unless she retracts something from what she gave up.
